title: Durable native worktree usage and explicit reviewed cleanup
scope: Durable physical-instance usage journal, clean-shutdown/history revision recovery floor, explicit live conversation owners, workspace reconnect history and seven-day snooze.
Native Source control review UI; checked-row confirmation; serialized no-force removal preserving branches and chats.
Worker repeats registration/status/merge/physical identity/branch/HEAD/mounted/permit checks. Managed directory parent authority is frozen at construction.
upstreamContractSummary: Source scans on startup, filters dismissed candidates for seven days, uses current mounted paths plus persistent workspace last-message history.
Source requires managed non-main registered attached worktree, clean known status, seven-day idle time when known, merged branch; fresh recheck per selected path.
Source preserves Git branches; explicit worktree deletion detaches workspace paths while retaining chats.

nativeBehavior.missingHistory: Imported unknown history never ages into permission by itself. Actual live use/new instance creates verified history.
nativeBehavior.journal: worktree-usage.json, 4 MiB/10,000 records, lifetime owner lock, QSaveFile revision checks, pinned Windows storage directory.
nativeBehavior.recovery: Missing, unclean, or differently revised conversation history starts a seven-day protection floor; corrupt/locked/externally changed journal disables cleanup.
nativeBehavior.identity: Windows FILE_ID_INFO volume/file IDs plus creation times for worktree root/common Git/admin dirs and exact .git/commondir/gitdir relationships.
nativeBehavior.explicitReview: Permit contains physical instance, reviewed branch+HEAD, exact durable journal hash and revocable owner/activity epoch. Boolean usageKnown cannot authorize cleanup.
nativeBehavior.lifecycle: Successful SessionStore save/commit hooks track explicit live owners; final close records final live use before clean journal commit. Archive/delete releases after host lifecycle transition.
nativeBehavior.snooze: Seven days per physical instance. Unknown records cannot be snoozed into authority.
nativeBehavior.cancel: Controller destruction revokes permit, cancels owned Git requests; pre-mutation cancellation produces no removal.
nativeBehavior.conflicts: Dirty/mounted/busy/main/detached/unmanaged/unregistered/future timestamp/locked/prunable/changed identity/changed HEAD or branch/stale history all reject.

reproducedDefects.failure: Clean close kept activation timestamp for long-lived background mounts.
reproducedDefects.fix: Record all verified currently live owner identities at shutdown before closeClean.

reproducedDefects.failure: A controlled real Git checkout after the last status subprocess changed to an unmerged branch; earlier code removed its directory.
reproducedDefects.fix: Review branch+HEAD binding and registration reread after status, then final comparison before Git removal.
reproducedDefects.fixture: Test executable forwards real Git and triggers only unique temporary repository actions.

reproducedDefects.failure: Retargeting managed-root to a junction made a previously used external worktree appear eligible. No external deletion was performed.
reproducedDefects.fix: Freeze canonical configured parent authority; refuse managed-root resolution changes. Preserve valid initially junctioned parent behavior.

limits: Not full Stagewise parity. Native usage is a conservative per-instance journal; source uses persistent multi-mount workspace history. Native still has one workspace per chat.
Review is opened explicitly; automatic source startup prompt and exact source prompt layout remain unimplemented. No automatic destructive cleanup.
Unknown imported history is more conservative than upstream null-last-use eligibility. Crash recovery adds a seven-day floor.
No automatic snooze record garbage collection is wired; records remain within explicit 10,000/4 MiB bounds and fail closed when full.
Windows physical identities implemented; unsupported platforms cannot authorize cleanup.

Git subprocess state checks and in-process repository locks do not form a filesystem/Git transaction against arbitrary external processes after the final check. Git no-force remains the final dirty/removal guard; no universal race-free guarantee.
A canceled Git process that already began mutation can have partial effects; this slice verifies cancellation before removal dispatch and before its final command.
Preserved reference/native-experiments source bytes remain unchanged. Production modules are separate adapted copies; the optional experiment target stays unlinked to ADE.
